mainTopic: Distances between walls, windows, gutters and dovecotes, the walking (דוושא) reason, and the rule that indirect damage (גרמא) is forbidden
overview: The גמרא explains the משנה about keeping a wall ארבע אמות from a neighbor's wall. רבא reads it as a wall that stood ארבע אמות away and fell. When it is rebuilt, it must stay that far, because people walking in the gap (דוושא) firm up the ground by the neighbor's wall. רב limits the rule to a garden wall, and רבי אושעיא applies it to a courtyard wall too. רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that they do not really argue: one speaks of an old city, the other of a new city. The גמרא then tests the walking reason against the rules about windows and roof gutters. It defends the reason by narrowing each case: a side wall near a window, and a sloping gutter. A new משנה requires a ladder to be kept away from a neighbor's dovecote so a mongoose cannot jump in. The גמרא shows this fits רבי יוסי and learns that even indirect damage (גרמא בניזקין) is forbidden. A story about רב יוסף's small palm trees begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First reading: a new wall must be kept four cubits away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first explains the משנה as talking about someone who comes to build a wall near his neighbor's wall. He must keep it ארבע אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to build a wall close to his neighbor's wall may not do so unless he keeps it four cubits away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first explanation of the משנה. It reads it as a rule about building a brand-new wall near a neighbor's wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the משנה is about the first time anyone builds next to the neighbor's wall. The rule is that the new wall needs a gap of ארבע אמות. The next step will challenge this reading from the משנה's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: to build close to, to put next to

phrases.english: One who comes to build a wall close by
phrases.notes: He means building close to a neighbor's existing wall.

phrases.english: may not build it close unless
he keeps it four cubits away from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא לִסְמוֹךְ, לֹא יִסְמוֹךְ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִרְחִיק מִמֶּנּוּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's explanation of the משנה, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person building a wall near his neighbor's wall must keep it ארבע אמות away.

steps.title: רבא objects from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה says 'one whose wall WAS near his friend's wall.' That means a wall was already standing there, so the case cannot be a brand-new wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: But the משנה says 'one whose wall was near his friend's wall'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the first reading. He argues that it does not match the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'whose wall was' describe a wall that already existed. The first reading treated the case as building for the first time, so it ignores this wording. רבא's point is that the reading must fit the language of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: but it teaches (introduces a quote that seems to contradict)

phrases.english: Rava challenged it:
But it says 'one whose wall was'
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה itself. The key word is 'was': a wall already stood there.

phrases.english: 'near his friend's wall' is what is taught!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first reading of the משנה (a brand-new wall)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording 'whose wall was' shows that a wall already stood there, so it cannot be describing the first time someone builds.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: a wall that fell
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the משנה. A wall stood ארבע אמות from the neighbor's wall and then fell. When it is rebuilt, it must still be kept ארבע אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what the משנה teaches: If someone's wall was near his friend's wall at a distance of four cubits, and it fell, he may not rebuild another wall close to it unless he keeps it four cubits away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the first reading with a new one that fits the words 'whose wall was.' The case is now about rebuilding a wall that collapsed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'was near' means the old wall stood there at a distance of ארבע אמות. The new point is that after the wall falls, he may not move it closer when he rebuilds. He must keep the same gap.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches (a rereading)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'near' (סָמוּךְ) in the משנה does not mean touching. It means the wall stood nearby, ארבע אמות away.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said, this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹתְלוֹ סָמוּךְ לְכוֹתֶל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: one whose wall was near his friend's wall
at a distance of four cubits, and it fell,
he may not build another wall close to it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִרְחִיק מִמֶּנּוּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: unless he keeps it four cubits away from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own objection by offering a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about building a new wall for the first time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about rebuilding a wall that stood ארבע אמות away and fell. The gap must be kept.

steps.title: Why must the gap be kept?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind keeping the ארבע אמות gap.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the rebuilt wall must stay ארבע אמות away. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is now clear, but its purpose is not. Knowing the reason will matter for the dispute about garden walls and courtyard walls later in this section.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the rebuilt wall must stay ארבע אמות away from the neighbor's wall

steps.title: Walking in the gap strengthens the ground
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that people walking in the space between the walls pack down the ground. That makes the foundation of the neighbor's wall stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the trampling here benefits there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that people walking in the open space help the neighbor's wall stay strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feet treading the ground make it firm, and this protects the neighbor's wall. If the new wall closes the gap, no one walks there anymore and the neighbor loses that benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason explains the coming dispute: it matters whether people already walk near the wall.

phrases.english: Because the trampling here
is good for there.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the neighbor's wall. People walking in the open space 'here' make the ground by that wall firmer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Walking in the gap firms up the ground and strengthens the neighbor's wall.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about rebuilding a fallen wall. The ארבע אמות gap must stay, because people walking there strengthen the neighbor's wall.

steps.title: רב: the rule is only for a garden wall
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ארבע אמות rule applies only next to a garden wall. Next to a courtyard wall, a person may build close.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They taught this only about a garden wall. But a courtyard wall: if he wants to build close, he may build close.
steps.whatsHappening: רב limits the משנה's rule to one kind of wall, a garden wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the trampling reason just given, the gap is needed next to a garden wall, where people do not usually walk. A courtyard is walked in all the time, so its ground is already firm, and רב allows building close.

phrases.english: Rav said:
They taught this only about a garden wall,
but a courtyard wall:
if he comes to build close, he may build close.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the limits of the rule just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארבע אמות gap is required only next to a garden wall, not next to a courtyard wall.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: the rule is for both walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא disagrees. He says the rule applies to a garden wall and a courtyard wall alike, so one may not build close to either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא says: Both a garden wall and a courtyard wall: if he wants to build close, he may not build close.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives the opposite view: there is no exception for a courtyard wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא holds that a courtyard wall also needs the gap. This looks like a direct argument with רב, which the next step will address.

keyTerms.meaning: both this and that, the same for each

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד כּוֹתֶל גִּינָּה וְאֶחָד כּוֹתֶל חָצֵר –
phrases.english: both a garden wall and a courtyard wall:
if he comes to build close, he may not build close.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד כּוֹתֶל גִּינָּה וְאֶחָד כּוֹתֶל חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that seems to disagree with רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארבע אמות gap is required next to both a garden wall and a courtyard wall.

steps.title: No real argument: old city versus new city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says רב and רבי אושעיא do not really disagree. רב is speaking about an old city and רבי אושעיא about a new city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: They do not disagree. This one is talking about an old city, and that one is talking about a new city.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא settles the apparent argument by placing each opinion in a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an old city the ground is already well packed, so a courtyard wall does not need the gap, as רב said. In a new city the ground is still soft, so even a courtyard wall needs the walking space, as רבי אושעיא said.
steps.whatToRemember: Next to a courtyard wall, the ארבע אמות gap is not needed in an old city but is needed in a new city. Next to a garden wall it is always needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
And they do not disagree:
this one is about an old city,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is רב, who allowed building close to a courtyard wall.

phrases.english: that one is about a new city.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is רבי אושעיא, who forbade it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי – הָא בְּעִיר יְשָׁנָה, הָא בְּעִיר חֲדָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two opinions in steps 6 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each opinion is about a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רבי אושעיא argue about courtyard walls.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב is talking about an old city with firm ground. רבי אושעיא is talking about a new city with soft ground.

steps.title: The משנה on windows and the ברייתא explaining it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a wall must be kept four cubits from a neighbor's windows: above, below, or opposite. It adds a ברייתא giving the reason for each direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: for windows, whether the wall is above, below, or opposite them, keep four cubits away. A ברייתא explains: above, so he cannot peek in and look; below, so he cannot stand on the wall and look; opposite, so he will not darken the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and a ברייתא about walls near windows. This is setting up a challenge against the trampling reason from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a separate reason for each direction. Two reasons are about privacy (peeking in), and one is about light (darkening). Notice that for the wall opposite the window, the only reason given is darkening. That detail is what the next step will use.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא was taught about it
He will peek or peer in

phrases.english: We learned: the windows,
phrases.notes: This means a new wall being built near a neighbor's windows.

phrases.english: whether from above, whether from below,
whether from opposite them – four cubits.
And it was taught about it:
above – so that he will not peer in and see,
below – so that he will not stand on it and see,
and opposite – so that he will not darken the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to test the trampling reason from Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall must be kept four cubits from a neighbor's windows on every side. Above and below, the reason is privacy; opposite, the reason is light.

steps.title: Only darkening is mentioned, not trampling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא gives only darkening as the reason for the wall opposite the window. If trampling were also a reason, it should have been mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason given is so he will not darken the house. But trampling is not given as a reason!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the trampling reason from Step 5. A wall opposite a window is also next to the neighbor's wall, so trampling should apply there too. Yet the ברייתא does not mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the gap exists so people walking there will pack down the ground near the neighbor's wall. A wall built opposite the window would also sit next to the neighbor's wall. So the ברייתא should have said trampling is a reason there too. Its silence suggests trampling is not a real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Trampling, people walking that packs down the ground

phrases.english: The reason is so that he will not darken,
but because of trampling – not!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲפִיל, אֲבָל מִשּׁוּם דַּוְושָׁא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in Step 9 against Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The trampling reason (דוושא) for the ארבע אמות gap given in Step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only darkening for the opposite wall. If trampling were a real reason, it would have been listed too.

steps.title: The case is a wall coming from the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a wall that comes toward the window from the side, at a right angle. In that case, trampling is not an issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A wall that comes in from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the trampling reason. It limits the ברייתא to a wall built at a right angle to the window's wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A side wall does not run along the length of the neighbor's wall. So it does not stop people from walking beside that wall, and trampling does not matter here. It can still block light coming into the window, and that is why darkening is the only reason the ברייתא gives.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
Coming from the side, a wall at a right angle

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture this wall as facing the window and running alongside it. It sticks out sideways from the neighbor's wall, near the window, like the letter T.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
With a wall that comes from the side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a side wall only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about any wall facing the window, so trampling should have been listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a side wall, where trampling does not apply. So the trampling reason stands.

steps.title: How far must the side wall be kept?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much distance is needed for a wall that comes in from the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how far must it be kept?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the case is a side wall, the גמרא asks how far from the window it must be built. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a side wall blocks less light than a wall directly facing the window, maybe it needs less distance. The גמרא wants the exact amount.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? (asking for a measurement)

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how far from the window must the side wall be built?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the side-wall case from Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required distance between a side wall and the neighbor's window.

steps.title: רב: the width of the window
steps.stepSummary: ייבא, quoting רב, says the side wall must be kept as far from the window as the window is wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: ייבא, the father-in-law of אשיין בר נדבך, said in the name of רב: the full width of the window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a measurement from רב. The side wall needs only as much space as the window's width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is much less than four cubits. Since a side wall blocks less light, a smaller gap is enough to let light reach the window.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as the full width of the window

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יֵיבָא, חֲמוּהּ דְּאַשְׁיָין בַּר נִדְבָּךְ,
phrases.english: Yeiva, the father-in-law of Ashyan bar Nidbakh, said,
in the name of Rav:
As the full width of a window.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר יֵיבָא, חֲמוּהּ דְּאַשְׁיָין בַּר נִדְבָּךְ, מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The side wall must be kept a distance equal to the window's width.

steps.title: He could still peek in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that at such a short distance, someone could stand on the wall and look into the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he can still peek in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's small measurement. The privacy concern from the ברייתא (Step 9) still seems to be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא worried that a person could stand on a wall and look in. A side wall only a window's width away seems close enough for that. So how can such a short distance be enough?

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, isn't it so? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But surely he can peek in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's measurement from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a window's width is enough distance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: So close a wall still lets someone stand on it and look in. That breaks the privacy concern from the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב זביד: the top of the wall is sloped
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that רב is talking about a wall whose top is built slanted, so nobody can stand on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: this is when he slopes the top of his wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד defends רב's measurement. It applies when the wall's top is made slanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the top of the wall slopes, a person cannot stand on it to look into the window. That removes the privacy worry, so the only concern left is light, and a window's width is enough for that.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
It is where he slopes his wall.
phrases.notes: He makes the top of the wall slanted, so nobody can stand up there and look in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: בְּמַדִּיר אֶת כּוֹתְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the wall has a sloped top.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The side wall has a flat top, so someone could stand on it and peek in.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wall's top is sloped, so no one can stand on it. A window's width is enough distance.

steps.title: But the משנה said four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה requires four cubits, not just the width of a window.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: four cubits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's measurement again. This time it uses the משנה quoted in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says four cubits for walls near windows. רב's measurement of a window's width seems to go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (challenging from a משנה)

phrases.english: But we learned: four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב's measurement from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a window's width is enough distance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires four cubits, which is much more than a window's width.

steps.title: One side versus two sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's measurement is for a wall on one side of the window. The משנה's four cubits is for walls on two sides of the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is a wall on one side; there it is walls on two sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by explaining that the two sources are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side wall leaves the window open to light from the other side, so a window's width is enough. If walls stand on both sides, much more light is blocked, so four cubits are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer that splits the cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A side wall near a window: on one side, keep it a window's width away (with a sloped top). On two sides, keep it four cubits away. The trampling reason from Step 5 stays standing.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, from one side,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is רב's ruling of a window's width; the second is the משנה's four cubits.

phrases.english: there, from two sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מֵרוּחַ אַחַת, כָּאן מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: one side versus two sides.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the משנה are talking about the same case, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means a wall on one side of the window; the משנה means walls on two sides, which need four cubits.

steps.title: The gutter rule seems to be about a ladder, not walking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source requiring four cubits between a wall and a roof gutter so a ladder can be set up. This suggests the four cubits are for the ladder, not for walking (דוושא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A wall must be four cubits from a roof gutter, so that he can stand up a ladder there. So the reason is the ladder, not walking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to challenge the earlier idea that four cubits between walls are needed for people to walk there (דוושא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source gives a reason for the four cubits: room for a ladder. If walking were a real reason for four cubits, the source should have mentioned it. Since it only mentions the ladder, it looks like walking is not a reason for keeping a distance.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking or trampling that packs down the ground

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַכּוֹתֶל מִן הַמַּזְחֵילָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: And the wall must be four cubits from the roof gutter,
so that he can stand up the ladder.
phrases.notes: The gutter's owner needs room to put up a ladder so he can clean and fix the gutter.

phrases.english: The reason is because of the ladder,
but not because of walking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to challenge the walking reason for the four-cubit distance.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the four-cubit gap is needed for walking (דוושא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source explains the four cubits only by the ladder. That suggests walking is not a reason for keeping a distance.

steps.title: It means a sloping gutter that sticks out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source is about a sloping gutter that sticks out past the wall. People can already walk underneath it, so only the ladder needs to be mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about here? A sloping gutter. If walking were the concern, a person can already walk back and forth under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the source is about a special kind of gutter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sloping gutter sticks out from the roof, so the ground under it can be walked on anyway. Walking does not need extra space there, so the only reason left for four cubits is the ladder. Walking can still be a reason in an ordinary case.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
With a sloping gutter,
for if the concern were walking,
he can already walk back and forth underneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a special case (a sloping gutter)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since only the ladder is mentioned, walking is not a reason for keeping a distance.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the case of a sloping gutter, walking is already possible underneath, so only the ladder needed to be mentioned. Walking can still be a reason in other cases.
steps.whatToRemember: The gutter source only mentions the ladder because it is about a sloping gutter, where people can already walk underneath.

steps.title: New משנה: ladder away from a dovecote, wall away from a gutter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a ladder must be four cubits from a neighbor's dovecote so a mongoose cannot jump in. A wall must be four cubits from a gutter so a ladder can be set up.
steps.simpleTranslation: One must keep a ladder four cubits away from a dovecote, so a mongoose cannot jump onto it. And a wall must be four cubits from a roof gutter, so that a ladder can be stood up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two rules about keeping a distance so you do not harm your neighbor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule protects the neighbor's birds: a mongoose could climb the ladder and jump into the dovecote. The second rule protects the neighbor's ability to fix his gutter. The second half is the same line the גמרא already quoted in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Mongoose or weasel, an animal that eats birds

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One must keep the ladder away from a dovecote
four cubits,
so that the mongoose will not jump.
phrases.notes: It could climb the ladder and jump into the neighbor's dovecote to eat the birds.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַכּוֹתֶל מִן הַמַּזְחֵילָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: And the wall must be four cubits from the roof gutter,
so that he can stand up the ladder.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַסּוּלָּם מִן הַשּׁוֹבָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with new distance rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder must be four cubits from a neighbor's dovecote, and a wall four cubits from a roof gutter.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי. He holds that each person may do what he wants in his own property, without keeping a distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יוסי? Because רבי יוסי says: This one digs in his own land, and that one plants in his own land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the ladder rule goes against the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds elsewhere that a person may plant a tree in his own field even near his neighbor's pit. Each one acts in his own property. By that logic, a person should be allowed to put a ladder in his own yard, so the משנה seems to disagree with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? The גמרא is suggesting an idea it may reject

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יוסי?
For if it were רבי יוסי, doesn't he say:
This one digs within his own land,
phrases.notes: This comes from a case of planting a tree near a neighbor's pit.

phrases.english: and that one plants within his own land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the new משנה follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ladder rule in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי lets each person act freely in his own property. So he should allow a ladder in one's own yard, and the משנה seems to disagree with him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees about damage from 'his own arrows'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבי יוסי. He agrees that one must keep a distance when the damage comes from his own action, and placing a ladder could let a mongoose jump right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי. רב אשי said that רב כהנא taught: רבי יוסי agrees about a person's own 'arrows'. Here too, sometimes just as he puts the ladder down, the mongoose is sitting in a hole and jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the משנה can fit רבי יוסי. He agrees that you cannot cause damage that comes directly from your own action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי only allows acting in your own land when the damage happens later on its own. If the damage comes right away from what you do, like shooting an arrow, even he forbids it. Putting up the ladder can let the mongoose jump immediately, so it counts as his 'arrows'.

keyTerms.meaning: His own arrows: damage that comes right away from his action

phrases.english: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי,
for רב אשי said:
When we were in the study hall of רב כהנא,
he would say:
רבי יוסי agrees about his own arrows;
phrases.notes: 'Arrows' means damage that comes straight out of what a person does, like shooting an arrow.

phrases.english: here too,
sometimes, just as he puts the ladder down,
the mongoose is sitting in a hole and jumps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by showing רבי יוסי can agree with the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case fits an exception that רבי יוסי himself accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי allows any action in one's own property, so he would allow the ladder.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי forbids damage that comes right away from one's own action. The ladder can cause such damage immediately.

steps.title: But the ladder only causes damage indirectly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ladder does not do the damage itself. The mongoose does, so this is only indirect causing (גרמא).
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is only indirect damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer: the ladder owner is not really the one doing the damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the mongoose jumps right away, the person only set up the situation. The animal does the damage. Damage you only set in motion like this is called גרמא, and it seems hard to call it a person's 'arrows'.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, an opening of a challenge
Indirect damage: causing harm without doing it yourself

phrases.english: But this is only indirect damage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that the ladder counts as his 'arrows'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that placing the ladder counts as damage from his own 'arrows'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mongoose does the damage, not the person. So it is only indirect (גרמא), and it should not be forbidden like direct damage.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the ladder is harmless. It is asking whether harm that a person only sets in motion is forbidden.

steps.title: Indirect damage is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי בר מתנה learns from the משנה that even indirect damage (גרמא) is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר מתנה said: This teaches us that causing damage indirectly is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב טובי בר מתנה accepts that this is גרמא and draws a rule from the משנה: even indirect damage is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is not pushed away. It becomes a lesson. Since the משנה requires keeping the ladder away even though the damage is only indirect, we learn that a person may not cause damage even indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us; a lesson drawn from the source

phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Mattana said:
This teaches us:
causing damage indirectly is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection that this is גרמא and turns it into a general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even indirect damage (גרמא) is forbidden, so the ladder must be kept four cubits from the dovecote.
steps.whatToRemember: The ladder case teaches a basic rule: גרמא בניזקין אסור. You may not even indirectly cause your neighbor damage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that indirect damage is forbidden, is a basic principle in the laws of neighbors and damages.

steps.title: The story of רב יוסף's small palm trees begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story: רב יוסף owned some small palm trees, and the sentence about them is just starting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף had some small palm trees, which were...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story about רב יוסף and his small palm trees. This line only sets the scene and gets us ready for what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a question or an answer. It is the opening of a real-life case that comes right after the rule about גרמא. The word דַּהֲווֹ tells us the description of the trees continues in the next words.

keyTerms.meaning: That were / which were (the sentence continues)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the point of the story yet. This line only says who and what. The problem with the trees is told in the words that follow.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef had
certain small palm trees, which were...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָנְהוּ תָּאלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after the conclusion that גרמא is forbidden, the גמרא begins a related story about רב יוסף's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only sets the scene: רב יוסף owned some small palm trees.
